# Brief — idea of the study (revision 4, after idea-review round 2)

## Question
With network interference, how accurate is the regression-based GATE estimator (fit outcome on functions of the assignment vector — own treatment, treated-neighbour fraction/count, higher-order terms — then predict at all-treated and all-control and difference; Chin 2019, Han & Ugander 2023)? What determines its error, and under which interference mechanisms, networks and designs does it hold, fail, or lose to the biased difference in means?

## Thesis (the claim the paper is built around)
The regression GATE estimator is limited by **extrapolation from the observed exposure distribution to the global-treatment and global-control corners**, and the two parts of its error — variance and bias — have *different* drivers that move in opposite directions with degree. A data-computable two-part diagnostic separates them and tells an experimenter when to trust the estimate, when a flexible learner cannot rescue it, and when the biased DM is the better choice. The extrapolation viewpoint itself is not new (Chin 2019 shows the feature distributions at global treatment/control differ from the observed one and invokes off-policy evaluation, qualitatively); the claimed contribution is the quantified, tested account, its interaction with the design, and the regime map including where regression loses.

### Notation
Features φ_i(z) (own z_i; treated-neighbour fraction f_i; optional count, 2-hop, interaction terms). τ̂ = Δxᵀβ̂ with Δx = mean_i[φ_i(1) − φ_i(0)] (the intercept cancels). Corner offsets: raw exposure distances of the corners from the observed exposure distribution, (1−p) for all-treated and p for all-control (fraction feature; mechanism-specific for count/2-hop).

### Predictions (fixed now; each falsifiable)
**Variance part.**
- *Leverage* L = Δxᵀ Σ̂_φ⁻¹ Δx, Σ̂_φ the empirical covariance of the feature rows under the observed assignment (pooled primary; the per-unit average of per-unit leverage is reported as variant for heterogeneous degree). For the fraction feature, L ≈ (1+d)/(p(1−p)) for features (own z, f), i.e. ∝ d/(p(1−p)) at large d; minimal at p = ½.
- P1. Where residuals are independent with variance σ², Var(τ̂) ≈ σ² L / n (OLS leverage; textbook, stated as the baseline, not the finding). The test is the *departure*: fit log-RMSE on log n, log d, log p(1−p) with CIs, on graphs where the iid formula is expected to hold (ER/SBM, Bernoulli) and where not (BA hubs, cluster designs, degree-correlated baselines, 2-hop features with shared neighbours); report where σ²L/n over- or under-states the realised variance and by what factor (an effective-n). **Bias part.**
- P2. For a response g(f) curved in exposure and a linear fit tangent near p, spillover bias ≈ −½g''(1−2p) to second order (zero at p = ½), plus a third-order term −(1/6)g'''[(1−p)³+p³]; it depends on *raw* distance × curvature and **not** on d (large d only narrows the observed support, so the bias neither grows nor shrinks with d for the fraction feature).
